media.title: Fold and Cut
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Fold and Cut

B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M1.S1.T1.C2.2D1
- Tool type: Exploration (the free first try, before the concept video)
- Textbook source: Class 5 Symmetrical Designs, the Alphabet Cutout activity (the letters A and H) and the opener questions on E N X T K V O (developer only). The letters C, U and F are practice values.

C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student finds that a letter with a line of symmetry can be cut out of folded paper by drawing only half (1/2) of it, and a letter with two lines by drawing only a quarter (1/4), because the folded halves match.
- Out of scope: turns and rotational symmetry, digits, designs made of several shapes, small or fancy letters.

D. TOOL DESCRIPTION

1. Opening Screen
- A top-down photo of a honey-coloured wooden desk. A green cutting mat holds a large square sheet of orange craft paper, about half the stage height on each side, with a faint outline of the capital letter A. A dashed vertical line and a dashed horizontal line cross the sheet through its middle, each with a round tab at both ends and a label, "vertical line" and "horizontal line". Silver scissors and a pencil lie at the lower right of the mat.
- Instruction line: "Which dashed line will you fold the paper on? Tap it."
- The child is invited to tap a dashed line. Goal chip: "Cut a full A".

2. Scene and Objects
- The sheet is open, folded in half (a half-size rectangle) or folded in quarter (a quarter-size square). A folded sheet shows the part to draw as a dotted outline and a round badge, "1/2" after one fold or "1/4" after two.
- A wooden shelf along the bottom holds the letter cards: one in Activities 1 to 5, seven in the star challenges. Each card is a cream square, about 8% of the stage width, with one plain bold capital; E, N, X, T, K, V and O are each in a different colour, as in the book.
- After a fold, two cards appear under the mat: "Full letter" and "Not the full letter".
- Star Challenge 2 only: two overlapping rings of string, the left labelled "Horizontal line", the right "Vertical line", the overlap "Both".

3. Main Interaction
- Tap a card on the shelf: its outline appears on a fresh open sheet.
- Fold: tap a dashed line and the paper flips over it (0.6 seconds). Tap the other line for a second fold (the one-fourth fold). Tap a folded line again to unfold it. At most 2 folds, on the two middle lines only.
- Guess: after a fold, tap "Full letter" or "Not the full letter". The scissors stay locked until then.
- Cut: tap the scissors. The pencil draws the dotted part solid, the scissors cut and the paper opens (4 seconds; 1.5 in the star challenges). The cutout is the drawn part plus its mirror image across each fold line. If it fills the pale outline of the letter exactly the outline glows green; if not, the parts that do not match pulse orange.
- Fold peek (Star Challenge 2): tap a letter on the mat, then a dashed line. Its halves slide over each other with no cutting; matching halves glow green, others pulse orange.
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" (opens the paper, clears the cut) and "Next" (locked until the activity is done); in the star challenges the right button reads "Check" until passed.

4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided, A). Goal line: "Fold the paper so the two halves of the A match, then cut." Goal chip: "Cut a full A". Setup: A outline, lines labelled. The child taps a line, a guess card, then the scissors. Guess: "Full letter" or "Not the full letter". Result: on the vertical line the badge reads "1/2", the full A opens and the outline glows green: "The left half and the right half of the A match, so drawing 1/2 gives the full A." Help: guided (labels, dotted part).
- Activity 2 (guided, H). Goal line: "Fold both ways and cut out the H." Goal chip: "Draw only 1/4". Setup: H outline, lines labelled. The child folds on both lines (badge "1/4"), guesses, cuts. Result: the full H opens: "The H has two lines of symmetry, so folding both ways and drawing 1/4 gives the full H." After one fold the H also opens whole, and the chip stays grey: "One fold works for the H too, but you drew 1/2. Fold both ways to draw only 1/4." Help: guided.
- Activity 3 (independent, C). Goal line: "Cut out a C. Find the fold that works." Goal chip: "Cut a full C". Setup: C outline, no labels. Result: the horizontal line gives "1/2" and a full C: "The top of the C and the bottom of the C match, so drawing 1/2 gives the full C." The vertical line gives a closed ring like an O: "The left half and the right half of the C do not match. This fold made an O, not a C." Help: independent.
- Activity 4 (independent, U). Goal line: "Cut out a U. Which fold works?" Goal chip: "Cut a full U". Result: the vertical line gives "1/2" and a full U: "The left half and the right half of the U match, so drawing 1/2 gives the full U." The horizontal line gives two tall bars: "The top of the U and the bottom of the U do not match." Help: independent.
- Activity 5 (independent, F). Goal line: "Try both lines on the F." Goal chip: "Try both lines". The child folds on the vertical line, guesses, cuts, presses Reset, then does the same on the horizontal line. Neither cutout is an F. Result after both: "Neither fold gave an F, so the F has no line of symmetry." Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 1 (the book's question).
  - Goal line: "Which of the following alphabet cutouts can be made by just drawing half (1/2) or quarter (1/4) of the letter? You can do it by drawing lines of symmetry on the letters." Goal chip: "Test 7 letters".
  - Setup: the shelf holds E, N, X, T, K, V, O. Guess: tap the letters you think can be made this way; each gets a pale ring. Then test each letter as in the activities, without guess cards. A letter that cuts out whole gets a green tick and its badge, "1/2" or "1/4"; a letter whose vertical and horizontal folds both fail gets a grey stamp, "no fold works". The rings may be changed; Check reads the rings.
  - Result: rings on E, X, T, K, V and O. Strip: "E, T, K and V have one line, so 1/2 is enough. X and O have two lines, so 1/4 is enough. N has no line of symmetry, so no fold works." Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 2 (the book's question).
  - Goal line: "Which of the letters have a horizontal line of symmetry? Which of the letters have a vertical line of symmetry? Which letters have both vertical and horizontal lines of symmetry?" Goal chip: "Sort 7 letters".
  - Setup: the two rings and the seven letters. Guess: drag every letter to where you think it belongs: left ring only, right ring only, the overlap, or outside both. Then use the fold peek to test and move any letter.
  - Result: E and K in the left ring only, T and V in the right ring only, X and O in the overlap, N outside. Read-outs fill in under the rings: "Horizontal line: E, X, K, O" "Vertical line: X, T, V, O" "Both: X, O". Help: independent.

5. Mathematical Understanding
- Folding and cutting makes the drawn part plus its mirror image: the whole letter only when the two halves match, and that is a line of symmetry. A letter can have a vertical line, a horizontal line, both, or none; one line needs 1/2 drawn, two lines need 1/4.

6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the outline glows green, the goal chip turns green with a gentle bounce, the pill gets a tick, and the strip gives the one-line why. A right guess of "Not the full letter" turns the strip green, with the why, but the chip stays grey until a full letter is cut. A wrong guess or answer gives a red strip, a small shake and one friendly line; retry is free.
- Mistake: guesses "Full letter" for a fold that is not a line of symmetry -> "The two halves of the [letter] do not match along this line, so it is not a line of symmetry. Try the other line." The parts that do not match pulse.
- Mistake: folds both ways on A, C or U -> "Both lines must be lines of symmetry to fold both ways. The [letter] has only one. Fold on that line." The second line pulses.
- Mistake: rings N, or expects an F cutout -> "No fold gave this letter. If the halves never match, there is no line of symmetry." The stamp pulses. A working letter left unringed -> "One letter that works has no ring. Look for a green tick."
- Mistake: a letter in the wrong place in Star Challenge 2 -> "The E has no vertical line. Peek at the vertical fold: do the halves match?"
- Hints, 3 levels: (1) "If you fold the letter on this line, will the two halves land exactly on each other?" (2) the tool slides the left half over the right half along the vertical line, then the top half over the bottom half along the horizontal line, 1 second each. (3) the line where the halves land exactly glows green: "Fold on the glowing line and draw the dotted part." For N and F no line glows: "Neither line makes the halves match."
- Edge cases: H, X and O also cut out whole with one fold (1/2 drawn); the strip then suggests folding both ways for 1/4. N and F have no line.

7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 is done when the rings are on E, X, T, K, V and O and all seven letters have a result; Star Challenge 2 when every letter is in its place.
- End screen: "Well done!" Remember: "A letter with a line of symmetry can be cut out by drawing only 1/2 of it." "A letter with two lines of symmetry can be cut by drawing only 1/4 of it." "If the halves do not match, the fold is not a line of symmetry." Think and talk: "Look at the first letter of your name. Can you cut it out by drawing only half? Why or why not?" Button: "Start again".

8. Assets and Language
- Images: top-down photo of a honey-coloured wooden desk; green cutting mat; orange craft paper (open, folded in half, folded in quarter); silver scissors and pencil cut-outs; loops of string. The letters are drawn in code as plain bold capitals, so folds and mirror images are exact. English only.

tool_config.idea: Find out by folding and cutting that a letter with a line of symmetry can be made by drawing only half of it (one fold) or a quarter of it (two folds), and that a fold on a line that is not a line of symmetry gives a cutout that is not the letter. This is the free first try of the chapter, so it asks and shows; the video that follows names the idea.
tool_config.title: Fold and Cut
tool_config.screen: Lali's craft table, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation, with the Happy Birthday wall banner behind it. A large square sheet of coloured paper lies in the middle of the table and is the largest thing on screen, with a dashed vertical fold line and a dashed horizontal fold line marked on it. On the left a shelf holds letter cards, each card a plain capital letter. A pair of scissors and a pencil lie beside the paper. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with progress dots under it. Controls: tap a letter card to put its outline on the paper; three fold buttons, Vertical, Horizontal and Both ways (one-fourth); a Draw button that shows the part of the letter to draw along the fold; a Cut button that cuts along the outline; an Open button that unfolds the paper and shows the cutout; a results sheet on the right with a row for each letter and three columns, horizontal line, vertical line and both, that the student ticks; Check, Hint, Retry (unfolds the paper for this card), Reset (clears the results sheet), Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: the fold chosen, the part drawn (1/2 or 1/4), a message under the opened paper saying whether the cutout is the full letter, and a card number out of 7.
feedback: After Open, a full letter shows a soft green message such as: The halves matched, so the cutout is the full A. A cutout that is not the letter shows a soft amber message such as: The two halves do not match, so this fold is not a line of symmetry. Try the other fold.
After Draw, the tool says how much of the letter is drawn, for example: You drew 1/2 of the letter. For the two-fold choice it says: You drew 1/4 of the letter.
A tick on the results sheet that does not agree with the cutouts slides back with a clue such as: Cut the letter with the Horizontal fold. Do the halves match?
On the card with the F, after every fold has been tried, the tool says: None of the folds gave an F, so the F has no line of symmetry.
tool_config.done_when: Every practice card is cut with a correct fold, the results sheet is ticked for the letters E, N, X, T, K, V and O, and the student has answered both of the story's questions from the sheet.

challenges: Card 1: cut the letter A. Choose the fold, then Draw, Cut and Open. Which fold do you use and how much of the A do you draw? Answer: the vertical fold, and half (1/2) of the A. The opened cutout is the full A.

Card 2: cut the letter H. Which fold do you use and how much of the H do you draw? Answer: fold both ways into one-fourth, once vertically and once horizontally, and draw a quarter (1/4) of the H. The opened cutout is the full H.

Card 3 (practice values): cut the letter M. Try the Horizontal fold first, then the Vertical fold. Answer: the Horizontal fold gives a cutout that is not an M, because the top and bottom of the M do not match. The Vertical fold gives the full M, with half (1/2) drawn.
Card 4 (practice values): cut the letter B. Which fold works? Answer: the Horizontal fold, with half (1/2) of the B drawn, because the top half and the bottom half of the B match.
Card 5 (practice values): try to cut the letter F with every fold. Answer: no fold gives an F, because the F has no line of symmetry. Its halves never match.

Challenge: 'Which of the following alphabet cutouts can be made by just drawing half (1/2) or quarter (1/4) of the letter? You can do it by drawing lines of symmetry on the letters. E N X T K V O' Cut each letter with the folds. Answer: E, X, T, K, V and O can be cut out, with 1/2 drawn for E, T, K and V and 1/4 drawn for X and O. N cannot, because it has no line of symmetry.

Challenge: 'Which of the letters have a horizontal line of symmetry? Which of the letters have a vertical line of symmetry? Which letters have both vertical and horizontal lines of symmetry?' Use your results sheet. Answer: horizontal line: E, X, K, O. Vertical line: X, T, V, O. Both: X, O.

hint_ladder.text: Look at the letter. If you folded it, would the two halves land exactly on each other?
Try the Vertical fold, then the Horizontal fold. After each one, look at the opened cutout and ask: is it the full letter?
For this letter, check one side against the other: which fold makes the two halves match?
Use the fold the tool shows, and draw only the part it outlines along the fold. The opened paper shows the full letter.

student_does: Look at the folded paper from the story, with half of the letter A drawn along the fold. Tap the line on the paper where it is folded, then press Next.
Choose a letter, choose a fold, press Draw, Cut and Open, and see whether the cutout is the full letter. Cut A with one fold, H with two folds, M and B with the right fold, and try F with every fold.

Answer the questions from the story: which of the letters E, N, X, T, K, V and O can be made by just drawing half or a quarter, and which have a horizontal line, a vertical line or both. Cut each letter and tick the results sheet.

content.publication_text: Which of the following alphabet cutouts can be made by just drawing half $(\frac{1}{2})$ or quarter $(\frac{1}{4})$ of the letter? You can do it by drawing lines of symmetry on the letters. The letters are E, N, X, T, K, V and O.

content.text:
1. A letter can be cut out from a folded paper only if it has a line of symmetry.
2. E has a horizontal line of symmetry. Fold the paper in half and draw $\frac{1}{2}$ of the E.
3. N has no line of symmetry. Its two halves never match, so N cannot be cut out by drawing half or a quarter of it.
4. X has a vertical and a horizontal line. Fold the paper into one-fourth and draw $\frac{1}{4}$ of the X.
[Image: Alphabet Cutout: Ans1: solution]
5. T has a vertical line. Fold the paper in half and draw $\frac{1}{2}$ of the T.
6. K has a horizontal line. Fold the paper in half and draw $\frac{1}{2}$ of the K.
7. V has a vertical line. Fold the paper in half and draw $\frac{1}{2}$ of the V.
8. O has a vertical and a horizontal line. Fold the paper into one-fourth and draw $\frac{1}{4}$ of the O.
9. Check: E, X, T, K, V and O have a line of symmetry, and N has none.
Answer: E, X, T, K, V and O can be cut out: $\frac{1}{2}$ for E, T, K and V, and $\frac{1}{4}$ for X and O. N cannot be cut out this way.
[Image: Alphabet Cutout: Ans1: solution (continued)]

E has a horizontal line of symmetry. Fold the paper in half and draw 1/2 of the E.

X has a vertical and a horizontal line. Fold the paper into one-fourth and draw 1/4 of the X.
T has a vertical line. Fold the paper in half and draw 1/2 of the T.
K has a horizontal line. Fold the paper in half and draw 1/2 of the K.

media.title: Turn and Check
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Turn and Check

B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M2.S5.T5.C14.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity
- Textbook source: Class 5 Symmetrical Designs, Let Us Make a Windmill Firki, Example 1 (the letter H turned, solved) and the turn table rows for I, X and Y (developer only). The flower, the letters N and L and the plus sign are practice values.

C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student turns a shape by 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn, checks each time whether it looks the same as at the start, and finds that a shape has rotational symmetry when it looks the same after a turn smaller than a full turn.
- Out of scope: lines of symmetry and folding, turns other than 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and full, digits, designs made of several shapes.

D. TOOL DESCRIPTION

1. Opening Screen
- A top-down photo: a round wooden turntable, about 60% of the stage height across, with a brass pin at its centre, on a pale linen cloth. Four brass notches on the fixed base, going round to the right from the top: "1/4" at the right, "1/2" at the bottom, "3/4" at the left and "Full" at the top beside a small red arrow. A curved arrow on the base shows that every turn goes to the right.
- On the turntable sits a four-petal flower of pink card with a green dot on the right petal. A thin dashed outline of the flower, fixed to the base, marks the starting position.
- Instruction line: "The green dot is on the right petal. Where will it be after a 1/4 turn? Tap a petal."
- The child is invited to tap a petal. Goal chip: "Follow the dot".

2. Scene and Objects
- The disc turns about the pin, only to the right. Every turn is measured from the start: a new stop first snaps the disc back (0.2 seconds), then turns it to the stop in 1 second. The dashed outline never moves.
- Turn row (Activity 2 on), along the bottom of the stage: four windows "1/4 turn", "1/2 turn", "3/4 turn", "Full turn", each with a snapshot of the shape after that turn and two buttons, "Same" and "Different"; plus a wider window "Rotational symmetry" with chips "Yes, at 1/4 turn", "Yes, at 1/2 turn" and "No".
- Shapes: pink flower (green dot on the right petal); gold card firki (four curved blades, red pin, green dot on the upper-left blade); blue N (green dot at the top-left end); orange L (green dot at the end of the foot); green plus sign (green dot on the top arm); the book's H (purple, red centre dot, white dots at the top of each stem), I (green bar, red centre dot), X (blue, red centre dot) and Y (tan, red dot at the end of the stem).

3. Main Interaction
- Activity 1: tap a petal as the guess; the disc then turns to the stop asked and the dot lands.
- From Activity 2: tap "Same" or "Different" under a window. That is the guess, and the disc at once turns to that stop. A shape that fits the dashed outline exactly looks the same; if a part sticks out it looks different. A right guess fills the window with the snapshot and turns the word green. A wrong guess leaves the disc at the stop with the parts that stick out shaded; the child reads the outline and taps again. Tap a notch to replay a turn without a guess.
- When all four windows are green, tap one chip in the "Rotational symmetry" window.
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" (disc back to the start, row cleared) and "Next" (locked until the activity is done).

4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided, flower). Goal line: "Follow the green dot. Tap the petal where it will be after a 1/4 turn." Goal chip: "Follow the dot". Guess: tap a petal; the question then moves to the 1/2 turn and the 3/4 turn. Result: the dot lands on the bottom petal, then the left, then the top; after a full turn the disc goes once round and the dot is back on the right. Strip lines: "A 1/4 turn moves the dot to the next petal, the bottom one." "A 1/2 turn is 1/4 + 1/4, so the dot is 2 petals on, at the left." "A 3/4 turn moves the dot 3 petals on, to the top." "A full turn is 4 quarter turns, so the dot is back at the start. The dot moved, but the flower looks the same." Help: guided, notches labelled.
- Activity 2 (guided, N). Goal line: "Turn the N. Does it look the same as the dashed outline?" Goal chip: "Fill the row". Setup: N on the disc, the outline labelled "start". Guess: "Same" or "Different" for each window. Result: 1/4 Different (the N lies on its side like a Z), 1/2 Same, 3/4 Different, Full Same; then the chip "Yes, at 1/2 turn": "The N fits the outline after a 1/2 turn, which is less than a full turn, so it has rotational symmetry." Help: guided.
- Activity 3 (independent, L). Goal line: "Fill the row for the L." Goal chip: "Fill the row". Result: Different, Different, Different, Same, and the chip "No": "The L fits the outline only after the full turn. A full turn always fits, so the L has no rotational symmetry." Help: independent.
- Activity 4 (independent, plus sign). Goal line: "Fill the row for the plus sign." Goal chip: "Fill the row". Result: Same in all four windows and the chip "Yes, at 1/4 turn": "The plus sign fits after a 1/4 turn, so it also fits after a 1/2 turn and a 3/4 turn. Its smallest turn is 1/4." Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 1 (the book's question).
  - Goal line: "Observe the dot in the firki. Does the firki look the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and a full turn?" Goal chip: "Check the firki".
  - Setup: the firki on the disc, the four windows only. Guess: "Same" or "Different" for each window. Result: Same in all four. Strip: "Yes, it looks the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn. The dot moves, but the firki looks the same." Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 2 (the book's table).
  - Goal line: "Observe the letters. Do they look the same when turned?" Goal chip: "Fill the rows: I, X, Y".
  - Setup: the H row is done for the child: Different, Same, Different, Same and "Yes, at 1/2 turn"; the child may tap its notches to watch. Small cards I, X and Y wait on a shelf above the row; tap one to put it on the disc, then fill its row as in Activity 2.
  - Results and strips: I: Different, Same, Different, Same, "Yes, at 1/2 turn": "The I is a bar. It lies flat after a 1/4 turn and fits again after a 1/2 turn." X: Same, Same, Same, Same, "Yes, at 1/4 turn": "The X fits after every turn, so its smallest turn is 1/4." Y: Different, Different, Different, Same, "No": "The Y fits only after the full turn, so it has no rotational symmetry." Help: independent.

5. Mathematical Understanding
- The child turns a shape and compares it with its starting outline. Looking the same means fitting the outline, whatever happens to the dot. Every shape fits after a full turn, so only smaller turns show rotational symmetry. 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2, so a shape that fits after a 1/4 turn also fits after a 1/2 turn.
- The child can say: "The dot moves, but I look at the shape." "A full turn always looks the same, so it does not count."

6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the window fills with the snapshot and its word turns green, the goal chip turns green with a bounce when the row is done, the pill gets a tick. A wrong guess or chip gives a red strip, a small shake and one friendly line; retry is free.
- Mistake: says "Different" because the dot moved -> "The dot moved, but look at the shape. It fits the dashed outline." The outline pulses.
- Mistake: says "Same" when a part sticks out -> "Look at the part that sticks out of the outline. The shape does not fit." That part pulses.
- Mistake: says "Different" for the full turn -> "After a full turn the shape is back where it started, so it always looks the same."
- Mistake: chooses "Yes, at 1/2 turn" for the X -> "The X already fits after a 1/4 turn. Pick the smallest turn that says Same."
- Mistake: chooses "Yes" for the L or the Y -> "Only the full turn said Same, and a full turn does not count. Look at the smaller turns." Chooses "No" for the N, I, H, X or plus sign -> "It said Same after a turn smaller than a full turn. That is rotational symmetry."
- Mistake: wrong petal in Activity 1 -> "A 1/4 turn moves the dot to the next petal, the way the arrow points. Count the petals." The next petal pulses.
- Hints, 3 levels: (1) "Look at the shape, not the dot. Does it fit its dashed outline?" (2) the disc turns to the next stop as a preview; parts that stick out are shaded orange, or the outline glows green if it fits. (3) the right button glows with "At this turn the [shape] fits the outline" or "does not fit the outline".
- Edge cases: the full turn is always Same. A "Yes, at 3/4 turn" chip is never offered, because a shape that fits after a 3/4 turn also fits after a 1/4 turn. The firki and the plus sign look the same everywhere, but the dot still moves.

7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 is done when all four firki windows are green; Star Challenge 2 when the rows of I, X and Y are green with the right chips.
- End screen: "Well done!" Remember: "A shape has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 turn." "The dot moves when you turn, but we look at the shape." "A full turn always looks the same, so it does not count." Think and talk: "If a shape looks the same after a 1/4 turn, will it also look the same after a 1/2 turn? Why?" Button: "Start again".

8. Assets and Language
- Images: round wooden turntable with a brass pin on linen; brass notches; paper firki on a stick (gold card, four curved blades, red pin, green dot); pink card flower; coloured card cut-outs of N, L, H, I, X, Y and a green plus sign, each with its dot. English only.

media.teaching_notes: Predict first: turn the letter H by a half turn. Does it look the same as before? Yes. After a 1/2 turn the H looks the same. A shape that looks the same after a turn smaller than a full turn has rotational symmetry. Every shape looks the same after a full turn, so a full turn does not count. The firki looks the same after a 1/4, a 1/2 and a 3/4 turn, so it has rotational symmetry. The letter H lies on its side after a 1/4 turn, so it looks the same after a 1/2 turn only. To check, put a dot on the shape, turn it a 1/4, a 1/2 and a 3/4 turn, and each time ask: does it look the same? You can cut out the shape and fix its centre with a nail, or use tracing paper. Rule: a shape has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after at least one of the turns 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4. 1. Z: put a dot on the top left of the Z. 2. After a 1/4 turn the Z lies on its side and looks like an N, so it does not look the same. 3. After a 1/2 turn the Z is upside down and looks the same, with the dot now at the bottom right. 4. After a 3/4 turn the Z lies on its other side and looks like an N again, so it does not look the same. 5. The Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn, so it has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn. 6. T: after a 1/4 turn the T lies on its side. After a 1/2 turn it is upside down, with the bar at the bottom. After a 3/4 turn it lies on its other side. None of these looks like the T, so the T has no rotational symmetry. 7. Check: every shape looks the same after a full turn, so the full turn does not count. Answer: The Z has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn. The T has no rotational symmetry

content.text:
Lali makes firkis for her friends. Follow the steps given below to make your own firki. 1. Take a square paper. 2. Fold the paper in half diagonally to make two triangles. 3. Open and fold it the other way to make two more triangles. 4. Open it again. You will see an 'X' shape on the paper. 5. Use scissors to cut along the four lines of the 'X'. Stop cutting about halfway to the centre. 6. Take one corner of each triangle and fold it gently towards the centre of the paper. Do not press it flat. 7. Fold every other corner towards the centre. 8. Push a pin through the folded corners and the centre of the paper. 9. Push the pin through a stick or straw.
Make sure the pin is not too tight. Check if your windmill spins when the wind is blowing.

content.text:
1. Predict first: turn the letter H by a half turn. Does it look the same as before?
2. Yes. After a 1/2 turn the H looks the same. A shape that looks the same after a turn smaller than a full turn has rotational symmetry.
3. Every shape looks the same after a full turn, so a full turn does not count.
4. The firki looks the same after a 1/4, a 1/2 and a 3/4 turn, so it has rotational symmetry. The letter H lies on its side after a 1/4 turn, so it looks the same after a 1/2 turn only.
5. To check, put a dot on the shape, turn it a 1/4, a 1/2 and a 3/4 turn, and each time ask: does it look the same? You can cut out the shape and fix its centre with a nail, or use tracing paper.
6. Rule: a shape has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after at least one of the turns 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4.

content.text:
Worked example: Does the letter Z have rotational symmetry? Does the letter T? Turn each one by 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4.
1. Z: put a dot on the top left of the Z.
2. After a 1/4 turn the Z lies on its side and looks like an N, so it does not look the same.
3. After a 1/2 turn the Z is upside down and looks the same, with the dot now at the bottom right.
4. After a 3/4 turn the Z lies on its other side and looks like an N again, so it does not look the same.
5. The Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn, so it has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn.
6. T: after a 1/4 turn the T lies on its side. After a 1/2 turn it is upside down, with the bar at the bottom. After a 3/4 turn it lies on its other side. None of these looks like the T, so the T has no rotational symmetry.
7. Check: every shape looks the same after a full turn, so the full turn does not count.
Answer: The Z has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn. The T has no rotational symmetry

media.title: Symmetry Sorter
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Symmetry Sorter

B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M2.S9.T9.C22.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity (sorting)
- Textbook source: Class 5 Symmetrical Designs, Let Us Do on the digits 1 to 0, the numbers 11 and 1001, and examples of 2-digit, 3-digit and 4-digit numbers (developer only). The letters C, Z, H, F, U, N, X, P and the numbers 906, 18, 181, 25 are practice values.

C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student runs a fold test and a turn test on a letter, digit or number and sorts it into reflection symmetry only, rotational symmetry only, both, or neither, and sees that the two tests can give different answers.
- Out of scope: turns other than 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4, fold lines on a slant, designs made of several shapes.

D. TOOL DESCRIPTION

1. Opening Screen
- A photo of a wooden sorting table in a school workshop. In the middle stands a pale wooden test bench with a white card in a clip frame, showing the capital letter C in large dark bold type, about 28% of the stage height. A shelf along the top holds three small cards, Z, H and F. Along the bottom stand four wooden crates, each about 20% of the stage width, with a picture, a name and a count badge showing 0: "Reflection only" (a card folded on a dashed line), "Turn only" (a round arrow), "Both" (the two pictures together) and "Neither" (a crossed circle).
- Instruction line: "Which crate will this card go in? Drag it there."
- The child is invited to drag the card on the bench into a crate as a guess. Goal chip: "Fill all 4 crates".

2. Scene and Objects
- Fold test: two round switches above the card, a dashed vertical line icon and a dashed horizontal line icon. A switch draws its line on the card; one half flips over the line like a page and lands on the other (0.8 seconds). If every part lands on a match the lamp turns green; parts that do not match glow orange.
- Turn test: a round brass knob at the right of the frame with a curved arrow pointing right. Each tap turns the card 1/4 to the right, leaving a dashed outline of the start, and lights the next lamp; the fourth tap is the full turn and returns the card to the start.
- Five lamps under the card, grey until tested: "Fold test": "vertical line", "horizontal line"; "Turn test": "1/4 turn", "1/2 turn", "3/4 turn". A lamp turns green with a tick (match, or looks the same) or shows a grey cross.
- Digit 1 is always a plain bar. Star Challenge 1 adds three read-outs under the crates: "Reflection symmetry:", "Rotational symmetry:", "Both:". Star Challenge 3 adds a number plate on the bench with a row of digit tiles 0 to 9 and tags "2 digits", "3 digits", "4 digits", and three boxes "Only rotational", "Only reflection", "Both" in place of the crates.

3. Main Interaction
- Tap a card on the shelf: it slides to the bench. Guess: drag the card into a crate; it rests on the rim with a "?" tag.
- Test: press "Test it". The card returns to the bench and the lamps not yet lit light one after another (1 second each). The child may also tap the switches and the knob by hand.
- Result: a right crate takes the card with a green tick and a bounce, and its count goes up by 1. A wrong crate sends the card back to the bench with all five lamps lit and one strip line; the child drags again. Drag a card out of a crate to remove it.
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" (empties the crates) and "Test it", which becomes "Next" when the activity is done. In Star Challenges 1 and 2 the right button reads "Check" and tests every card in the crates at once; wrong cards bounce back.

4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided, C, Z, H, F). Goal line: "Test each card, then sort it." Goal chip: "Fill all 4 crates". Setup: the opening scene, with a caption under each crate: "fold works, turn does not", "turn works, fold does not", "both work", "neither works". Guess: the crate. As each lamp lights the strip names it ("Vertical line: no match."). Results: C goes to "Reflection only" ("The horizontal fold matches, but no turn makes the C look the same, so the C is Reflection only."); Z to "Turn only" ("No fold matches, but the Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn."); H to "Both" ("The H matches on both fold lines and looks the same after a 1/2 turn."); F to "Neither" ("No fold matches and no turn makes the F look the same."). Help: guided.
- Activity 2 (independent, U, N, X, P). Goal line: "Sort these 4 cards. Test each one." Goal chip: "Sort 4 cards". Setup: the four cards on the shelf, no captions. Results: U "Reflection only" ("The U matches on the vertical line and never looks the same after a turn."); N "Turn only" ("The N has no matching fold, but it looks the same after a 1/2 turn."); X "Both" ("The X matches on both lines and looks the same after every turn."); P "Neither". Help: independent.
- Activity 3 (independent, numbers). Goal line: "A number is tested as a whole. Sort these 4 numbers." Goal chip: "Sort 4 numbers". Setup: the cards 906, 18, 181, 25, each number on one card. Results: 906 "Turn only" ("After a 1/2 turn the 9 becomes a 6 and the 6 becomes a 9, and they swap places, so 906 looks the same. No fold matches."); 18 "Reflection only" ("The horizontal fold matches, but a 1/2 turn would make 18 read 81."); 181 "Both" ("181 matches on the vertical line through the 8 and looks the same after a 1/2 turn."); 25 "Neither". Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 1 (the book's question).
  - Goal line: "Find symmetry in the digits." The three questions follow: "Which digits have reflection symmetry?" "Which digits have rotational symmetry?" "Which digits have both rotational and reflection symmetries?" Goal chip: "Sort 10 digits".
  - Setup: the shelf holds the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0 in the book's colours. Guess: drag every digit to a crate and press Check; wrong digits bounce back with a line, and can be tested and dragged again.
  - Result: Both: 0, 1, 8. Reflection only: 3. Turn only: empty. Neither: 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9. Read-outs: "Reflection symmetry: 0, 1, 3, 8" "Rotational symmetry: 0, 1, 8" "Both: 0, 1, 8". Strip: "6 and 9 turn into each other, so neither looks the same by itself. The 3 has a horizontal line only." Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 2 (the book's question).
  - Goal line: "Now, let us look at the following numbers: 11 and 1001. Do these have rotational symmetry, reflection symmetry or both symmetries?" Goal chip: "Test 2 numbers".
  - Setup: cards 11 and 1001. Guess: drag each to a crate, press Check. Result: both go to "Both": "11 and 1001 match on a vertical line and look the same after a 1/2 turn, so both numbers have both symmetries." Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 3 (the book's question).
  - Goal line: "Give examples of 2-digit, 3-digit and 4-digit numbers which have rotational symmetry, reflection symmetry, or both." Goal chip: "Fill 3 boxes".
  - Do: tap a box (the guess), tap a tag for the digits, then tap tiles to fill the slots (0 is locked in the first slot). When the last slot is filled the tool tests the whole number: if it fits the chosen box it drops in with a tick; otherwise the plate clears and the strip says "[number] has [reflection symmetry only, rotational symmetry only, both or neither], so it does not go in this box."
  - Done when each box holds a number and the numbers include a 2-digit, a 3-digit and a 4-digit one. Help: independent.

5. Mathematical Understanding
- Two tests: does a line make the halves match, and does the card look the same after a 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 turn. A card can pass one, both or neither, so both tests are run every time. A number is tested as a whole: the digits also swap places when it turns.

6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the card drops into its crate with a green tick and a bounce; the goal chip turns green when the activity is done. A wrong crate gives a red strip, a small shake and one friendly line; retry is free.
- Mistake: card that matches on a fold put in "Both" -> "A line of symmetry is not a turn. Run the turn test: does the [card] look the same after a turn?" The turn lamps pulse.
- Mistake: card that fits a turn but has no fold put in "Neither" or "Reflection only" -> "Turning is not folding. The [card] does not match when folded, but it looks the same after a turn." The matching turn lamp pulses.
- Mistake: 6 or 9 put in a turn crate -> "A 1/2 turn makes the 6 look like a 9, so the 6 does not look the same by itself." The bench card turns and shows a 9 over the dashed 6.
- Mistake: 3 put in "Neither" -> "Fold the 3 on the horizontal line. The top half lands on the bottom half." The horizontal lamp pulses.
- Mistake: tests a number digit by digit -> "A number is tested as a whole. After a 1/2 turn the digits also swap places."
- Mistake: Test it with no guess -> "First drag the card to the crate you think is right."
- Hints, 3 levels: (1) "Which test says yes for this card: the fold test, the turn test, or both?" (2) the tool runs the five lamps on the bench. (3) the right crate glows with its caption.
- Edge cases: the bar 1 passes both fold lines and the 1/2 turn; the 3 passes the horizontal fold only (its 1/2 turn looks like a backwards 3); 0 and 8 pass both tests; "Turn only" stays empty for the digits.

7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 is done when all ten digits are in the right crates; 2 when 11 and 1001 are in "Both"; 3 when the boxes are filled.
- End screen: "Well done!" Remember: "Two tests: fold it, and turn it." "A shape can pass the fold test, the turn test, both, or neither." "6 and 9 turn into each other, so neither looks the same by itself." Think and talk: "The 3 passes only the fold test, but the 8 passes both. What is different about them?" Button: "Start again".

8. Assets and Language
- Images: wooden sorting table; four wooden crates with picture labels; pale wooden test bench with a clip frame; brass knob; two round switches; white cards. Letters, digits and numbers are drawn in code as plain bold type. English only.

tool_config.idea: Test a letter, a digit or a number with a fold line and with a turn, and sort it into reflection only, turn only, both, or neither, so that the student sees that the two tests give two different answers and runs both every time.
tool_config.title: Symmetry Sorter
tool_config.screen: Lali's craft table, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. A wooden test board in the middle holds one large card at a time, the largest thing on screen, with a letter, a digit or a number on it. Beside the board are two testers. The fold tester has two switches, Fold on the vertical line and Fold on the horizontal line, which draw a dashed line on the card and slide one half over the other so the student sees whether the halves match. The turn tester is a turn dial with three stops, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4, which turns the card to the right and keeps a dashed outline of the starting position. Under the board four trays stand in a row: Reflection only, Turn only, Both and Neither. A shelf above holds the cards still to be tested. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with progress dots under it. Controls: tap a card to bring it to the board; tap a fold switch; tap a stop on the dial; drag the card into a tray; Check, Hint, Retry (returns the card to the board), Reset (empties the trays), Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs under the board: Vertical line: halves match or do not match; Horizontal line: halves match or do not match; 1/4 turn, 1/2 turn, 3/4 turn: looks the same or looks different; and the number of cards in each tray.
feedback: After the two tests the tool shows a soft green message when the tray fits, for example: The halves match on the horizontal line and the card never looks the same after a turn, so it is Reflection only. A card in the wrong tray slides back with a clue such as: Run the turn test. Does it look the same after a 1/2 turn?
For the digit 6 the tool says: A 1/2 turn makes the 6 look like a 9, so the 6 does not look the same by itself.
For a number the tool shows the whole number on the board and folds the whole number, not each digit alone.
The tray counts update after every card, so the student can see which group is still empty.
tool_config.done_when: Every practice card is in the right tray, the digits are sorted, the numbers 11 and 1001 are tested, and the student has made a number for each group.

Card 2 (practice values): the letter Z. Run both tests and choose a tray. Answer: no fold matches, but after a 1/2 turn it looks the same, so Z goes in Turn only.
Card 3 (practice values): the letter H. Run both tests and choose a tray. Answer: the vertical and the horizontal fold both match and it looks the same after a 1/2 turn, so H goes in Both.
Card 4 (practice values): the letter F. Run both tests and choose a tray. Answer: no fold matches and no turn makes it look the same, so F goes in Neither.

Card 5 (practice values): sort four cards together: the letter U, the letter S, the plus sign and the letter P. Answer: U goes in Reflection only, S in Turn only, the plus sign in Both, and P in Neither.

Challenge: 'Find symmetry in the digits.' The digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 0 are on the shelf, with the digit 1 drawn as a plain bar. 'Which digit(s) have reflection symmetry? Which digit(s) have rotational symmetry? Which digit(s) have both rotational and reflection symmetries?' Answer: reflection symmetry: 0, 1, 3, 8. Rotational symmetry: 0, 1, 8. Both: 0, 1, 8. The digits 6 and 9 turn into each other, so neither looks the same after a 1/2 turn by itself.

Challenge: 'Now, let us look at the following numbers: 11, 1001. Do these have (a) rotational symmetry, (b) reflection symmetry or (c) both symmetries?' Then: 'Give examples of 2-, 3-, and 4-digit numbers which have rotational symmetry, reflection symmetry, or both.' Answer: 11 and 1001 have both symmetries. Sample examples: rotational symmetry only 69, 619, 6969; reflection symmetry only 38, 383, 3883; both 88, 808, 8118. Your examples may differ.

media.title: M, S and the plus sign: which test do they pass
media.context: Concept image for the teaching concept Reflection Only, Turn Only or Both. It uses the plan's own M, S and plus sign (practice values), not the letters or digits of the book's questions.
media.composition: Three cards in a row, one sign on each with its dashed lines or its curved turn arrow, and a caption under each.
media.description: Three cards: the letter M with a dashed vertical line, the letter S with a curved arrow for a 1/2 turn, and a plus sign with dashed lines and a curved arrow for a 1/4 turn.

content.text:
1. The digit $1$ is drawn as a plain bar, so test the digits as they are drawn in your maths book.
2. Reflection: fold each digit along a vertical or a horizontal line. $0$, $1$ and $8$ match on both lines, and $3$ matches on a horizontal line. $2$, $4$, $5$, $6$, $7$ and $9$ match on no line.
[Image: Let us do: Ans1: solution]
3. Rotation: turn each digit a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. $0$, $1$ and $8$ look the same. A $\frac{1}{2}$ turn turns $6$ into $9$ and $9$ into $6$, so $6$ and $9$ do not look the same by themselves. $2$, $3$, $4$, $5$ and $7$ do not look the same.
4. Both: the digits in both lists are $0$, $1$ and $8$.
5. Check: $3$ is in the first list only, and $6$ and $9$ are in neither list.
Answer: (a): $0$, $1$, $3$, $8$; (b): $0$, $1$, $8$; (c): $0$, $1$, $8$

4. Both: the digits in both lists are $0$, $1$ and $8$.
5. Check: $3$ is in the first list only, and $6$ and $9$ are in neither list.
Answer: (a): $0$, $1$, $3$, $8$; (b): $0$, $1$, $8$; (c): $0$, $1$, $8$

1. The digit $1$ is drawn as a plain bar. Test each number with a fold line and with a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn.
2. $11$: fold along the vertical line between the two bars and the halves match. Turn it a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn: the two bars swap places and the number looks the same.

media.title: Design Studio
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Design Studio

B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M3.S11.T11.C31.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity (building and testing designs)
- Textbook source: Class 5 Symmetrical Designs, Making Designs, Let Us Think and Let Us Do with squares and triangles (developer only). The designs in Activities 1 to 3 are practice values.

C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student adds and colours parts so that a design looks the same after a 1/2 turn or a 1/4 turn, sees that colours count, and finds the lines of symmetry of a design by folding.
- Out of scope: turns other than 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4, fold lines other than the vertical, horizontal and two diagonal lines.

D. TOOL DESCRIPTION

1. Opening Screen
- A top-down photo: a round pale-wood board, about 60% of the stage height across, on blue felt, with a brass pin at its centre. On the pin sits a blue square with one sand equilateral triangle against its left side, tip pointing left, and faint "+" sockets on its other three sides.
- Instruction line: "Make the design look the same after a 1/2 turn. Where will the triangle land? Tap a place."
- The child is invited to tap a free "+" socket. Goal chip: "Same after a 1/2 turn".

2. Scene and Objects
- Tray at the lower right: 6 blue squares, 6 sand equilateral triangles of the same side, 3 blue circles, and paint pots orange, blue, green, pink.
- Turn dial above the board, stops "1/4", "1/2", "3/4". A stop shows faint ghost copies of the parts where they would land: a ghost on the same shape and colour glows green, any other ghost gets a red outline.
- Four dashed fold lines through the pin (vertical, horizontal, two diagonals), a tab at each end. A tab flips one half over the line: matching parts glow green, others pulse orange.

3. Main Interaction
- Drag a piece to a "+" socket and it snaps there; in the free build (Star Challenge 3) it snaps edge to edge against a placed piece. Drag a piece back to the tray to remove it. Tap a triangle to turn it round. Tap a paint pot, then a part, to colour it. Tap a dial stop for ghosts, a fold tab for a fold.
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" and "Check", which becomes "Next" when the activity is done.

4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided, half turn). Goal line: the opening instruction line. Goal chip: "Same after a 1/2 turn". Guess: tap the "+" where the triangle will land. The dial turns to "1/2": the ghost lands on the right, tip pointing right, red outlined. The child drags a triangle there and presses Check. Result: "After a 1/2 turn the triangle on the left lands on the right, so the design needs 1 + 1 = 2 triangles." Help: guided.
- Activity 2 (guided, quarter turn). Goal line: "Make the design look the same after a 1/4 turn." Goal chip: "Same after a 1/4 turn". Setup: a blue circle on the pin, one blue square touching it at the top, four "+" sockets. Guess: "How many squares will the design have? Tap 2, 3 or 4." The child taps the stops 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 (the top square's ghost lands on the right, bottom, left), drags 3 squares there and presses Check. Result: "The top square lands on the right, the bottom and the left, so the design needs 1 + 3 = 4 squares." Help: guided, ghosts on tapping a stop.
- Activity 3 (independent, colours and lines). Goal line: "Do colours matter? Find out." Goal chip: "Test the square". Setup: a square cut by one diagonal, top-left to bottom-right, into an upper-right orange triangle and a lower-left blue triangle. Guess: "Yes" or "No" for "Does it look the same after a 1/2 turn?", and tap the dashed lines you think are lines of symmetry. Check shows the 1/2 turn and all four folds. Result: No; only the other diagonal is a line: "Only 1 line works. The cutting line is not one, because orange would land on blue." Help: independent.
- Star Challenge 1 (the book's question, Making Designs).
  - Setup: a blue circle on the pin; a triangle above and one below, tips touching the circle; a triangle left and one right, flat sides against the circle, tips out; a second circle touching the right tip. "+" sockets mark the left, top and bottom tips.
  - (a) Goal line: "Does the design have rotational symmetry? Yes/No." Goal chip: "Test the design". Guess: tap "Yes" or "No", then the dial. Result: No: "After a 1/2 turn the circle on the right lands on the left, where there is no circle."
  - (b) Goal line: "Try to change the design by adding some shapes so that the new design looks the same after a 1/2 turn." The child drags a circle to the left tip and presses Check; any additions that make every ghost at 1/2 land on a match pass. Saved as B.
  - (c) Goal line: "Now try to modify or add more shapes so that the new design looks the same after 1/4 turn." Starting from B, the child turns the top and bottom triangles round and drags circles to their tips; Check passes when every ghost at 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 lands on a match. Saved as C.
  - (d) Goal line: "Do the new designs have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw the lines of symmetry." The child taps the dashed lines for B, then for C. Expected: B has 2 lines (vertical, horizontal), C has 4 (those and the two diagonals).
- Star Challenge 2 (the book's question, Let Us Think).
  - Part 1 Goal line: "Does this design look the same after 1/2 turn? Does the design look the same after 1/4 turn?" Setup: 4 squares in a 2 by 2 block, green top left and bottom right, pink top right and bottom left. Guess: "Yes" or "No" for each turn, then the dial. Result: 1/2 Yes, 1/4 No: "After a 1/2 turn green lands on green and pink on pink. After a 1/4 turn green lands on pink."
  - Part 2 Goal line: "Colour the square given in the figure using two colours so that the design looks the same after every 1/4 turn. How many times does this shape look the same during a full turn?" Setup: a white square with two diagonals and two middle lines dashed: 8 triangles round the middle. The child colours them with two pots and presses Check; only colours that take turns pass (orange, blue, orange, blue all round). Then the child taps "2", "4" or "8". Result: 4: "A 1/4 turn moves each triangle on 2 places, onto its own colour. 8 ÷ 2 = 4 times in a full turn."
  - Part 3 Goal line: "Do these designs have reflection symmetry also? Draw the line(s) of symmetry." Setup: the green and pink block, then the child's coloured square, with a chip "No line of symmetry". Result: the block has 2 lines, the two diagonals; the coloured square has none: "Every dashed line would put orange on blue, so there is no line of symmetry." Help (Star Challenge 2): independent.
- Star Challenge 3 (the book's question, squares and triangles).
  - Part 1 Goal line: "Make different symmetrical designs by using these two shapes." Goal chip: "Keep 3 designs". Setup: free build, 6 squares and 6 triangles. Check tests the turns and four fold lines: a design with a symmetry becomes a thumbnail in a "my designs" strip along the bottom and the board clears (a design that matches a kept one when turned or flipped does not count as different); otherwise "This design has no turn or line of symmetry yet. Try changing it."
  - Part 2 Goal line: "Does this shape have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw its line(s) of symmetry. Does it have rotational symmetry? If yes, at which turn? Does it have both symmetries?" Setup: 4 blue squares in 2 rows of 2, a sand triangle at each end of each row, tips out. The child taps the lines and turn stops that work (or "No turn"), then "Yes" or "No" for both symmetries. Result: 2 lines (vertical, horizontal); rotational symmetry at 1/2 turn; both symmetries.
  - Part 3 Goal line: "Now, make your designs. Sort your designs in 3 categories: designs with only rotational symmetry, designs with only reflection symmetry, and designs with both rotational and reflection symmetry." Setup: the thumbnails and three boxes, "Only rotational", "Only reflection", "Both". The child drags each design to a box and presses Check; wrong ones bounce back. Every box needs a design; a "+" tile reopens the board. Help: independent.

5. Mathematical Understanding
- Copy every part to the place where it would land; colours count too. Lines of symmetry are found by folding; a design can have a turn only, a line only, both, or neither.

6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: ghosts glow green, the goal chip turns green with a bounce, the pill gets a tick. A wrong answer gives a red strip, a small shake and one friendly line; retry is free.
- Mistake: taps a socket where the triangle does not land in Activity 1 -> "After a 1/2 turn the triangle goes to the opposite side of the square." The right socket pulses.
- Mistake: a part has no partner -> "After a 1/2 turn this triangle lands here, and nothing is there. Add a copy of it." The red outline pulses.
- Mistake: ignores colour -> "The shape matches, but the colour does not. Colours count." The two parts pulse.
- Mistake: taps a line that is not a line of symmetry -> "Orange lands on blue along this line, so it is not a line of symmetry. A turn is not a fold."
- Mistake: answers 8 for the full turn -> "8 is the number of triangles. Count the turns that look the same." Uses one colour, or more than two -> "Use two colours, and let them take turns round the square."
- Hints, 3 levels: (1) "After the turn, where does each part land? Is there a part there already?" (2) the dial shows the ghosts. (3) the missing part appears faintly in the red outlined place.
- Edge cases: a design may pass a 1/2 turn but not a 1/4 turn; a triangle on a square has a line but no turn; a strip of 4 triangles has a turn but no line.

7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 is done when (a) to (d) pass; 2 when its three parts pass; 3 when 3 designs are kept, the four-square shape is answered and every box holds a design.
- End screen: "Well done!" Remember: "To make a design look the same after a turn, copy each part to where it lands." "Colours count as well as shapes." Think and talk: "Can a design look the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn? Show one." Button: "Start again".

8. Assets and Language
- Images: pale-wood board with a brass pin on blue felt; wooden tray; four paint pots; cut-out blue squares, sand equilateral triangles and blue circles. English only.

tool_config.idea: Add, change and colour parts of a design so that it looks the same after a 1/2 turn and after a 1/4 turn, and find its lines of symmetry with a fold line, so that the student sees where each part lands after a turn and that colours count.
tool_config.title: Design Studio
tool_config.screen: Lali's craft table, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. A large round design board with a pin at its centre and four faint guide marks, at the top, right, bottom and left, fills the middle and is the largest thing on screen. A tray beside it holds 6 light blue squares and 6 pink equilateral triangles with the same side as the squares, the pieces of the book's sheet of shapes, and circles for the book's design, and two pots of colour. A turn dial with three stops, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4, sits in front of the board. A fold line tool offers four lines, vertical, horizontal and the two diagonals. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with progress dots under it. Controls: drag a shape from the tray onto the board; tap a placed shape to turn it a quarter; tap a colour pot and then a part to colour it; choose a stop on the dial to show faint ghost copies of the design where each part would land after that turn, with a red outline round any part that has no partner; choose a fold line to show one half folded over the other and whether the shapes and colours match; Undo, Check, Hint, Retry (clears the design of this card), Reset (empties the board), Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: the number of shapes on the board, the turn chosen, and for each fold line, matches or does not match, with a card number out of 7.
feedback: The ghost copies show where each part lands after the chosen turn. A part with no partner gets a red outline and the tool says: After a 1/2 turn this triangle lands here, and nothing is there. Add a copy of it in that place.
When every part has a partner the tool says in green: Every part lands on a matching part, so the design looks the same after this turn.
A fold line shows the two halves folded over each other. If a shape or a colour does not match, the tool marks it and says, for example: Orange lands on blue, so this line is not a line of symmetry.
When a design is finished the tool shows its result for the turns and the lines, and the student sorts it into only rotational symmetry, only reflection symmetry or both.
tool_config.done_when: Every practice design looks the same after the asked turn, the book's designs are made and tested, and the student has sorted at least three designs into the three groups.

challenges: Card 1 (practice values): a circle with one triangle above it, pointing up. Add a shape so that the design looks the same after a 1/2 turn. Answer: add a triangle below the circle, pointing down. The design then has 2 triangles and no red outlines after the 1/2 turn.

Card 2 (practice values): from the design of card 1, add shapes so that it looks the same after a 1/4 turn. Answer: add a triangle on the left, pointing left, and one on the right, pointing right. The design then has 4 triangles and looks the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn, which is 4 times.

Card 3 (practice values): a strip of 2 squares side by side. Colour the left square orange and the right square blue, then test the 1/2 turn. Answer: after a 1/2 turn the orange square lands on the blue square's place, so the design does not look the same. Colour both squares orange and it does. Colours count.

Card 4 (practice values): a square cut by its two diagonals into 4 triangles. Colour the top and bottom triangles orange and the left and right triangles blue. Test the turns and the four fold lines. Answer: it looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn. The vertical and horizontal fold lines match, and the diagonals do not. It has 2 lines of symmetry.

Challenge: Making Designs. The design is a circle in the middle with a triangle above and below it, each with its point touching the circle, a triangle on the left and right, each with its flat side touching the circle, and a second circle at the point of the right triangle. '(a) Does the design have rotational symmetry? Yes/No. (b) Try to change the design by adding some shape(s) so that the new design looks the same after a 1/2 turn. (c) Now try to modify or add more shapes so that the new design looks the same after 1/4 turn. (d) Do the new designs have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw the lines of symmetry.' Answer: (a) No. (b) add a circle at the left tip. (c) make the four arms equal, with a circle at each tip. (d) yes: 2 lines for (b), 4 lines for (c). Your designs may differ.

Challenge: Let Us Think. 'Does this design look the same after 1/2 turn? Does the design look the same after 1/4 turn?' for the square of four smaller squares, green at the top left and bottom right and pink at the other two. 'Colour the square given in the figure using two colours so that the design looks the same after every 1/4 turn. How many times does this shape look the same during a full turn?' 'Do these designs have reflection symmetry also? Draw the line(s) of symmetry.' Then the squares and triangles: 'Make different symmetrical designs by using these two shapes', the shape of four squares with a triangle at each end of each row, and 'Sort your designs in 3 categories'. Answer: the green and pink square: 1/2 turn yes, 1/4 turn no, with 2 lines of symmetry, its two diagonals. The coloured square: alternate the two colours on the 8 triangles, 4 times in a full turn, and no line of symmetry. The shape of four squares: 2 lines and a 1/2 turn, both symmetries. Sample designs may differ.

hint_ladder.text: Look at the design. After the turn, where does each part land? Is there a part there already?
Choose the turn on the dial. A red outline shows the place that has no partner. What is missing there?
Put a copy of the missing part in the place with the red outline. Then turn again and check the next part.
Add the part the tool shows in the red outlined place. Every part now has a partner, so the design looks the same after the turn.

1. The two designs are the green and pink square and the square coloured orange and blue.

Answer: Green and pink square: yes, $2$ lines (the two diagonals). Orange and blue square: no line of symmetry.

media.teaching_notes: Predict first: a wooden block has a design carved on it. The print on the cloth shows only half of the design, cut by a straight edge. Where is the other half? Block printing is a traditional craft of Rajasthan, known for beautiful patterns and bright colours. Artisans use carved wooden blocks to print designs on fabric. Many blocks have a line of symmetry. A half print has one straight edge, and that edge is the line of symmetry. The other half is the same picture on the other side of the line, as if the print were folded along it. To match a block to a half print, find the block's line of symmetry, imagine cutting the block along it, and look for the half print with the same shapes along its straight edge. Rule: the two halves of a symmetrical print are the same shape on the two sides of the line of symmetry. 1. The half print has one straight edge. That edge is the line of symmetry. 2. The straight edge runs down the middle of the leaf, along the stem. 3. Draw the same half on the other side of the line, as if the paper were folded along the edge. 4. The two halves together make the whole leaf. 5. Check: fold the whole print along the line and the two halves land on each other. Answer: The whole print is the half print together with its copy on the other side of the straight edge

7. Check: five blocks and five prints, and each print is used once.

content.text:
1. The design B is made of $4$ hearts placed round the middle.
2. Turn it a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn: the top heart lands where the right heart is, the right heart where the bottom heart is, and so on. The design looks the same after every $\frac{1}{4}$ turn.
3. The dashed vertical line and the dashed horizontal line are lines of symmetry: the left half matches the right half, and the top half matches the bottom half.
[Image: Block Printing: Ans1: solution]
4. So the design has rotational symmetry and reflection symmetry.
5. Check: it looks the same after a turn and it has lines of symmetry, so it has both.
Answer: Every $\frac{1}{4}$ turn. It has both rotational symmetry and reflection symmetry.

content.text:
1. Test each shape with a fold line (reflection symmetry) and with a turn (rotational symmetry). The shapes are numbered $1$ to $19$ round the border from the top-left corner, going to the right, then down, then to the left, then up.
2. Shape $1$, three pink triangles touching at their corners: $3$ lines of symmetry, and it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
[Image: Let us do: Ans1: solution]
3. Shape $2$, the green six-pointed star: $6$ lines, and it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{6}$ turn. Tick and star.
4. Shape $3$, the yellow six-sided shape: it has a vertical line and a horizontal line of symmetry, and it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
5. Shape $4$, three lilac circles joined to the middle, drawn nearly even: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
6. Shape $5$, the green triangle with grey corners: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
7. Shape $6$, the pink rectangle: $2$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
8. Shape $7$, the grey diamond: $2$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
9. Shape $8$, the five-sided shape with equal sides: $5$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{5}$ turn. Tick and star.
10. Shape $9$, the lilac ring of small triangles, drawn nearly even: $5$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{5}$ turn. Tick and star.
11. Shape $10$, the seven-sided shape with equal sides: $7$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{7}$ turn. Tick and star.
12. Shape $11$, the blue shape of four triangles: $4$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn. Tick and star.
13. Shape $12$, the pink triangle with three teal circles: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
14. Shape $13$, the orange slanted four-sided shape: no line of symmetry, but it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Star only.
15. Shape $14$, the yellow triangle with three small grey triangles: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
16. Shape $15$, the thin pink triangle with a square corner: no line of symmetry and no turn that works. No mark.
17. Shape $16$, the two maroon triangles touching at their points: $2$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
18. Shape $17$, the circle: every line through the middle is a line of symmetry, and it looks the same after every turn. Tick and star.
19. Shape $18$, the blue square: $4$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn. Tick and star.
20. Shape $19$, the purple triangle with three equal sides: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
21. Check: $17$ shapes get a tick mark, all except $13$ and $15$, and $18$ shapes get a star mark, all except $15$. $17 + 2 = 19$ and $18 + 1 = 19$.
Answer: Tick mark (reflection symmetry): all shapes except $13$ and $15$. Star mark (rotational symmetry): all shapes except $15$.

topics.summary: The chapter's ideas in one walk round Lali's craft table: lines of symmetry and cutouts, turns and rotational symmetry, telling the two apart in letters, digits and numbers, designs that look the same after a turn, and block prints.

content.text:
1. Predict first: you have walked round the whole craft table. Can you say one idea from each stop, from the folded paper to the block prints? Read the lines below and tick each idea you remembered.
2. Line of symmetry: a line that splits a shape into two halves that match when the shape is folded along it. A letter with one line of symmetry can be cut out of folded paper by drawing 1/2 of it, and a letter with two lines by drawing 1/4 of it.
3. Check: the letter A has a vertical line, so draw 1/2 of the A along the fold. The letter H has two lines, so draw 1/4 of the H.
4. A horizontal line goes across and a vertical line goes up and down. A letter can have a horizontal line, a vertical line, both or none.
5. Turns: a full turn is four quarter turns, and 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1. Two quarter turns make a 1/2 turn.
6. Rotational symmetry: a shape looks the same after a 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 turn. The firki does. The letter H does after a 1/2 turn. The letter Y does not.
7. Check: does the letter Z look the same after a 1/2 turn? Yes. After a 1/4 turn? No.
8. Two tests: fold for reflection symmetry and turn for rotational symmetry. M has reflection symmetry only, S has rotational symmetry only, and the plus sign has both.
9. Digits: 0, 1 and 8 have both symmetries. 3 has reflection symmetry only. 6 and 9 turn into each other, so neither looks the same after a 1/2 turn by itself.
10. Designs: to make a design look the same after a 1/2 turn, give every part a matching part on the opposite side. For a 1/4 turn, give every part a matching part on all four sides. Colours count too.
11. Check: a square of 4 smaller squares, green at the top left and bottom right and pink at the other two, looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn.
12. Block prints: the straight edge of a half print is the line of symmetry. A block stamped 4 times, a 1/4 turn each time, makes a print that looks the same after every 1/4 turn.
13. Check: a flower block stamped 2 times with a 1/2 turn between looks the same after a 1/2 turn.

modules.module_summary: Making designs that look the same after a turn and finding their lines of symmetry, block printing, shapes on the border, a project with vegetable blocks, and a revision of the whole craft table.

objectives.objective_text: Students fold a paper along a line of symmetry and draw half or a quarter of a letter along the fold to make the full letter cutout.
Students name the horizontal and the vertical lines of symmetry of a letter and say which letters have both lines.
Students find which letters can be cut out by drawing half or a quarter, and name the letters with a horizontal line, a vertical line or both lines of symmetry.
Students describe a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn, and say where a dot on a turning shape lands after each turn.
Students turn a shape by 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 and decide whether it has rotational symmetry by checking if it looks the same after a turn.
Students say whether the firki and the letters H, I, X and Y look the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn, and name the turn of their rotational symmetry.
Students use a fold test and a turn test to decide whether a letter or sign has reflection symmetry only, rotational symmetry only, both or neither.
Students find the digits and numbers with reflection symmetry, rotational symmetry or both, and give examples of 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers of each kind.
Students add shapes to a design so that it looks the same after a 1/2 turn and after a 1/4 turn, and count the turns at which the design matches in a full turn.
Students check shapes and colours to find whether a design looks the same after a turn, and find its lines of symmetry by folding.
Students change and colour designs so that they look the same after a 1/2 turn and a 1/4 turn, and draw the lines of symmetry of the designs.
Students match a wooden block to its half print by finding the line of symmetry along the straight edge of the print.
Students explain why a block stamped 2 times with a 1/2 turn, or 4 times with 1/4 turns, makes a print that looks the same after that turn.
Students match blocks to their half prints, name the turn and the symmetry of a block print, mark border shapes for reflection and rotational symmetry, and plan a vegetable-block project.

Book item: Look at the letters E, N, X, T, K, V and O. (a): Which of the letters have a horizontal line of symmetry? ___; (b): Which of the letters have a vertical line of symmetry? ___; (c): Which letters have both vertical and horizontal lines of symmetry? ___

Book item: Observe the dot in the firki. Does the firki look the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and a full turn? ___

Book item: Observe the letter H. Dots have been marked on it to keep track of its orientation. Does the H look the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn? Does it have rotational symmetry? Yes/No.

Does it have rotational symmetry (Yes/No)?

Book item: Find symmetry in the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0. (a): Which digit(s) have reflection symmetry? ___; (b): Which digit(s) have rotational symmetry? ___; (c): Which digit(s) have both rotational and reflection symmetries? ___
Book item: Now, let us look at the following numbers: 11 and 1001. Do these have (a): rotational symmetry, (b): reflection symmetry or (c) both symmetries?
Book item: Give examples of 2-, 3-, and 4-digit numbers which have rotational symmetry, reflection symmetry, or both.

Book item: (a): Does the design have rotational symmetry? Yes/No. (b): Try to change the design by adding some shape(s) so that the new design looks the same after a 1/2 turn. Draw the new design in your notebook. (c): Now try to modify or add more shapes so that the new design looks the same after 1/4 turn. Draw the new design in your notebook. (d): Do the new designs have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw the lines of symmetry.
Book item: Look at the design made of 4 squares. Does this design look the same after 1/2 turn? ___ Does the design look the same after 1/4 turn? ___
Book item: Colour the square given in the figure using two colours so that the design looks the same after every 1/4 turn. How many times does this shape look the same during a full turn?
Book item: Do these designs have reflection symmetry also? Draw the line(s) of symmetry.
Book item: Cut out squares and equilateral triangles with the same side length. These are provided at the end of the book. Make different symmetrical designs by using these two shapes.
Book item: Does this shape have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw its line(s) of symmetry. Does it have rotational symmetry? If yes, at which turn? Does it have both symmetries?

Book item: Now, make your designs. Sort your designs in 3 categories: designs with only rotational symmetry, designs with only reflection symmetry, and designs with both rotational and reflection symmetry.
Book item: Below are images of wooden blocks and a part of their prints. Match each block to its correct print by drawing a line. One is done for you.
Book item: The design B looks the same after every ___ turn. This design has ___ symmetry.

chapter_approach.intro: The chapter takes place at Lali's craft table. Paper cutouts, a windmill firki, wooden printing blocks and cards of letters and digits show what a line of symmetry is, what it means for a shape to look the same after a turn, and how to tell the two apart. A short video explains each idea, and an interactive tool lets the student try it alone.

points.text: Every idea has one short concept video. The tool that follows is where the student explores, builds and checks the idea alone, with hints, retry and reset. Four tools, each with its own purpose, follow the chapter's own plan.
points.title: Videos teach, tools explore

points.text: Each tool opens with a short recall of the video idea, then lets the student play and apply it, and ends with the chapter's own question, used exactly as the book gives it.
points.title: A tool in three steps

points.text: Every solved example, Let Us Do question and every answerable prompt of the book is its own short video with a step by step solution and a question picture and a solution picture, in a Questions topic that follows the idea it practises.
points.title: Every book question has its own video

points.text: A fold line tests reflection symmetry and a turn tests rotational symmetry. A shape can pass one, both or neither, so the student runs both tests every time.
points.title: Two tests for symmetry

points.text: Letters, digits, designs and block prints are the book's own. Any shape or number the plan adds is a practice value and is said to be one.
points.title: Only the book's shapes
